quotes.text: The tasks are drawn from the clinical database MIMIC-IV version 2.2 (snapshot released in January 2023, hosted on PhysioNet)
every task record stores the identifier of its source patient record, so any task can be traced back to its origin

rationale: Dataset name, version, snapshot date, platform and a task-to-source-record route are all stated in S1. The TREC snapshot date (27 April 2021) is also pinned.

quotes.text: Data access: HuggingFace gated under OpenRAIL (CT-RATE).

rationale: Origin of each source dataset and the terms or gating (OpenRAIL, PhysioNet, Redivis credentials) are documented. No consent, IRB status or explicit 'not required' statement appears in S1-S3, so only origin plus one other element is present.

quotes.text: Selection: The 10 tasks are selected to cover disease categories with a range from single disease to multiple diseases.

rationale: A selection and sampling design is stated (also tumor-size ranges for slides), but no comparison against a named target population is given.

quotes.text: The benchmark includes a safety test suite that measures unsafe outputs such as contraindicated medication orders
a separate bias test that compares agent accuracy across patient demographic groups

rationale: S1 (Appendix Z) states both an unsafe-output test suite and a separate bias test across demographic groups.

quotes.text: To limit contamination, the test split is held out and distributed only through gated access
we measured verbatim overlap between the test tasks and a public web corpus, finding no exact matches

rationale: A developer-side control (held-out, gated split) is paired with a measured overlap check.

quotes.text: Test-label isolation: test labels are never committed to git; bootstrap writes them to a /tests/ mount that main does not see.

rationale: S1 states the agent cannot reach gold at run time and names mechanisms (no mount, credential held only by bootstrap, labels not public). The same pattern is given for CT, X-ray and trial matching.

quotes.text: Environment components are fixed at release: database snapshot, software image, and patient-simulation LLM are each version-pinned.
During evaluation, only the model under test is called; no other external services are involved.

contradiction_quotes.text: During evaluation, only the model under test is called; no other external services are involved.

rationale: S1 reports pinned data, software and judge with no live external call besides the model under test, so the reported score is 2. S4 compose config for X-ray tasks passes live OpenAI judge credentials to the verifier, and the README names a configurable GPT-5.4 judge, so a contradiction flag is raised for verification.

quotes.text: Solvability was confirmed by executing a scripted reference solution for every task through the grader.
All 120 reference implementations received correct grades.

rationale: A scripted reference solution is run through the grader and the result is reported. The count of 120 does not match the 54 tasks; noted but the anchor is met.

quotes.text: (a) default config is byte-identical to upstream
unnecessary or unsafe writes are penalised in the score

rationale: Tasks change state (output files, configs, writes), so NA does not apply. S1 shows an unchanged-state check only for EHR Format Conversion plus a general penalty on unnecessary writes, so coverage is partial. The S4 code comment claiming the grader checks all other records unchanged does not count as reporting (G1a).

quotes.text: Random-action agents achieve 3.1% success across tasks.

rationale: An empirical random-agent success rate is reported; S1 also gives a design argument (random-guess success typically below 10%).

quotes.text: Random-action agents achieve 3.1% success across tasks.

rationale: A random agent's score is reported 'across tasks'. The sentence sits in the E.7 tags block, so scope to all 54 tasks is stated only by the words 'across tasks'; scored on that wording.

quotes.text: Solvability was confirmed by executing a scripted reference solution for every task through the grader.
All 120 reference implementations received correct grades.

rationale: Reference-solution evidence supports the deterministic verifiers, but there is no validation of the grader on incorrect outcomes and no agreement or error figures for the LLM judge used for X-ray correction.

quotes.text: All runs use temperature 0 and a fixed random seed, and each task is run three times

rationale: S1 states temperature 0, a fixed seed and a three-run repeated-run policy; the main text also reports 3 attempts.

quotes.text: Task success rate across all 54 × 3 trials (Wilson 95% CI), with cost and time per task.

rationale: A Wilson 95% CI is shown for success rates in the README chart, but no test of the model-comparison claims is reported. The paper's 'significantly' wording carries no test.

quotes.text: Across 3 attempts on 54 tasks (i.e 162 trials)
All runs use temperature 0 and a fixed random seed
specifies how many independent times each task is run

rationale: Run count (3 per task), seed/temperature policy and independence of attempts are all stated on S1/S2.

quotes.text: Task success rate across all 54 × 3 trials (Wilson 95% CI), with cost and time per task.

rationale: A CI on headline success rates with trials as the unit is stated in S2. Clustering of tasks within patients, templates or categories is not addressed.

quotes.text: we ran each task eight times and report pass^8, the fraction of tasks solved in all eight runs
together with the agreement of the final environment state across the eight runs

rationale: An all-runs pass^k metric and final-state agreement across reruns are reported with the run count (eight).

quotes.text: with xhigh reasoning effort with disabled web browsing capabilities

rationale: Reasoning effort and temperature 0 are stated. Model names (e.g. Opus-4.8, GPT-5.5) are family-level, and the S4 snapshot IDs (gpt-4o, claude-3-5-sonnet) differ from the S1 models, so identifiers count as absent. The README gives only a Harbor dependency pin (0.8.0), not a harness tag matched to the results.

quotes.text: Tools are specified using JSON schemas with name, arguments, and types.
Documentation for each tool declares whether it reads or modifies state
Agent prompts include these tool descriptions.

rationale: S1 states schemas, read/write declarations and return/error semantics for every tool, and says agent prompts include the descriptions. No S5 chunks are in the packet to confirm this, so s5_reach rests on the S1 statement.

quotes.text: We ran conformance tests confirming that each tool behaves as documented.
Two tools are simulated stubs that return fixed placeholder responses
also stated in the tool descriptions shown to the agent

rationale: Conformance tests, disclosure of two stubbed tools and disclosure to the agent are all stated in S1. S5 chunks are absent, so s5_reach rests on the S1 statement.

quotes.text: The write actions that change patient state (medication orders, notes and messages) are listed in a table.
Writes are executed against a sandboxed copy of the record, and unnecessary or unsafe writes are penalised in the score.
The agent prompt states that writes are sandboxed.

rationale: Write actions are listed, execution is sandboxed and unsafe or unnecessary writes are penalised. S1 says the agent prompt states the sandboxing; S5 chunks are absent so this is not independently confirmed.

quotes.text: (d) per-shard parquet row counts and canonical content hashes match the gold summary.

rationale: Grader inputs are named (output state, submitted answer files, LLM judge votes for X-ray). No rationale is given for the LLM judge, and there is no validation on labelled correct and incorrect outcomes with error rates.

quotes.text: Agents have no web access during runs and retrieval tools are restricted to the task environment
A private held-out split with hidden labels is kept off all public surfaces
every released task carries a canary string

contradiction_quotes.text: Agents have no web access during runs and retrieval tools are restricted to the task environment

rationale: Leakage controls, a private held-out split and a canary are all reported. S4 task configs set allow_internet = true (S1 Appendix B also says the container has internet), which conflicts with the 'no web access' wording, so a contradiction flag is raised for verification.

quotes.text: Accuracy is reported by task family (diagnosis, ordering, documentation) and by patient subgroup (sex, race)
with case counts displayed for every slice in the tables

rationale: S1 states results per task family and per patient subgroup with case counts for each slice. Per-category results (Table 4) and task counts (Table 2) are also given, though the paper's own tables show no sex or race slices.

quotes.text: Data access: Public (MIMIC-IV demo + synthetic errors).
Data access: Redivis-gated (Stanford STARR via EHRSHOT).
(Hugging Face, OpenRAIL gated). Accept the dataset agreement

rationale: Record source is stated as real data with synthetic injected errors (mixed). Credentialing and agreement requirements document governance, and per-dataset terms are given separately from the repo code. The data-terms element (iii) is the weakest of the three.
